title: Naturality and independence of the smooth purity map
statement:
In the situation of [thm-pur-finite-coefficient-smooth-purity],
the smooth purity map $\gamma_{f,K}$ of
[def-pur-smooth-purity-map] is natural in $K$, and it is
independent of the choices made in its construction.

proof.text:
Fix the finite coefficient ring $A=\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ and the smooth separated $f:X\to Y$ of pure relative dimension $d$ in the statement. Write $M_K=Lf^*K$, $T=\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$, and $\omega=Rf^!\Lambda_Y$. By [def-pur-smooth-purity-map], the map is $\gamma_K=\theta_K(1_{M_K}\otimes\Pi_f^{-1})\tau_K$, with the specified canonical orientation $\Pi_f:\omega\xrightarrow{\sim}T$. We first check naturality of $\theta$. By [def-pur-co-smoothness], its adjoint is the map $a_K:Rf_!(M_K\otimes^L\omega)\to K$ obtained successively from symmetry, $\operatorname{PF}_{f,\omega,K}^{-1}$, $\varepsilon_{f,\Lambda_Y}\otimes1_K$, and the left unitor. For any $u:K\to K'$ in $D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ put $m=Lf^*u$. Naturality of the projection isomorphism in [fix-prop-projection-formula], and of the tensor symmetry and unitors, gives
$$u\,a_K=a_{K'}\,Rf_!(m\otimes1_\omega).$$
Here the counit at $\Lambda_Y$ is a fixed morphism, so the counit part of this equality is simply $(\varepsilon\otimes1_{K'})(1\otimes u)=(1\otimes u)(\varepsilon\otimes1_K)$. Taking adjoints through the natural Hom bijection of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] gives
$$Rf^!u\,\theta_K=\theta_{K'}(m\otimes1_\omega).$$
The tensor formula of [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness] ensures that these specified maps are isomorphisms on precisely the smooth finite-coefficient domain being used; no adjunction on arbitrary unbounded pro-etale objects is needed.

source.place: First sentence: naturality of the tensor formula; expanded using the adjoint formula (Scholze, Six-Functor Formalisms, Definition 5.1, p. 32).

proof.text:
The other two squares are formal. Let $L=\Lambda_X(d)$, so that $K(d)$ means tensor with this fixed sheaf by [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. The map $\tau_K$ in [def-pur-smooth-purity-map] is the canonical identification $(M_K\otimes^L L)[2d]\to M_K\otimes^L L[2d]$. On a K-flat tensor model it identifies each summand indexed by $(p,q)$ with the same summand after the shift. The total differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] is $d_P\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_L$; since $L$ is in degree zero and $2d$ is even, both shifted differentials agree. This identity commutes with every map in the first factor. It therefore descends to the canonical derived shift identification, and is natural for derived morphisms (equivalently, apply the identity to the arrows in a roof, then invert its quasi-isomorphism). Thus
$$\tau_{K'}(m\otimes1_L)[2d]=(m\otimes1_T)\tau_K.$$
By the bifunctor law [lem-weil-derived-tensor-functorial], the two composites that apply $m$ in the first factor and $\Pi_f^{-1}$ in the second are equal:
$$(m\otimes1_\omega)(1\otimes\Pi_f^{-1})=(1\otimes\Pi_f^{-1})(m\otimes1_T).$$
Both are exactly $m\otimes\Pi_f^{-1}$. The orientation is fixed with $f$, and does not vary with $K$.

source.place: First sentence: twist reassociation and tensoring the fixed orientation; explicit naturality squares.

proof.text:
Paste the three equations of steps 1 and 2. With right-to-left composition they read
$$\begin{aligned}
Rf^!u\,\gamma_K
&=\theta_{K'}(m\otimes1_\omega)(1\otimes\Pi_f^{-1})\tau_K\\
&=\theta_{K'}(1\otimes\Pi_f^{-1})(m\otimes1_T)\tau_K\\
&=\gamma_{K'}(m\otimes1_L)[2d].
\end{aligned}$$
This is the required naturality square for every morphism $u:K\to K'$; it is an equality of morphisms, not merely an isomorphism of their sources and targets.

source.place: First sentence: compose the three naturality squares.

proof.text: For independence, first keep the prescribed normalization of the orientation. The factor $\Pi_f$ is the canonical isomorphism of [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object], as specified in [def-pur-smooth-purity-map]. Its geometric construction uses the normalized DNC comparison: [thm-pur-dnc-invariance] says that the isomorphism of section invariants which is the identity on standard pairs is unique. Hence two choices of etale coordinates producing that comparison give the same morphism. The base $X$ of the normal bundle is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; the field $k$ is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and $k$. The prime $\ell$ is invertible on $X$, since $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. The vector-bundle integration used on the normal-bundle side is likewise the unique map restricting to the specified affine-space trace on every trivializing open, by [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity]; replacing a trivializing cover or a bundle frame cannot replace that map. These are precisely the local choices in the diagonal/DNC construction named by the canonical orientation theorem. In particular we use its specified canonical $\Pi_f$, and no selection of an arbitrary isomorphism $\omega\cong T$.

source.place: Second sentence: canonical diagonal orientation, DNC uniqueness and the normalized vector-bundle comparison.

proof.text: Changing a K-flat representative of $M_K$ does not change the tensor factors as derived objects: [lem-weil-derived-tensor-resolution-independent] supplies their canonical comparison, with identity and cocycle laws, without assuming a direct chain map between arbitrary K-flat resolutions. Under these comparisons the arrows tensoring $\Pi_f^{-1}$ are the same bifunctorial arrow by [lem-weil-derived-tensor-functorial]. The shift reassociation is also the same: the summand identification in step 2 commutes with every tensor-model comparison arrow, hence with roofs and their inverses. Thus both the first and the middle factors in the composite defining $\gamma_K$ are unaffected by resolution choices, after the specified canonical identifications.

source.place: Second sentence: independence of tensor and twist models, using the ringed-site comparison rather than an unjustified direct lift.

proof.text: Finally the adjoint formula $a_K$ of step 1 fixes the last factor uniquely: an adjunction Hom bijection is injective, so two candidates with that same adjoint equal $\theta_K$. If a compactification or an etale-origin witness used to realize the operation is changed, [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] identifies the Hom bijections canonically, independently of the witness and compatibly with compactification comparisons. The projection formula [fix-prop-projection-formula] is compatible with these compactification comparisons as well. The symmetry, fixed counit and unitors in $a_K$ are therefore identified with the same adjoint composite. Injectivity again identifies the resulting $\theta_K$. Together with steps 4 and 5 this identifies each of the three factors, hence their composite $\gamma_K$. For three choices the comparisons agree by the cocycle laws already cited, so the independence assertion is coherent and introduces no extra normalization.

source.place: Second sentence: independence of the adjoint tensor map and hence of the composite.
